old.title: Bone Mass Measurement (DXA) (Synthetic)
verification_notes: Synthetic fictional policy generated from a scenario specification; not CMS guidance.

sections.heading: Indications for Coverage
sections.text:
Bone mass measurement is covered when the requirements of this policy are met.
- Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism.
- Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture.
- Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for estrogen-deficient women at clinical risk for osteoporosis.

sections.heading: Medical Necessity Criteria
sections.text:
The beneficiary must meet each of the following criteria:
1. The beneficiary is at least 60 years of age.
2. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period.
3. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of osteoporosis.

sections.heading: Limitations and Exclusions
sections.text:
The following limitations apply:
1. Bone mass measurement is not covered when performed only to confirm a prior result from a different modality.
2. Peripheral bone density testing used only for screening is not covered.
3. Bone mass measurement is not covered for beneficiaries without a qualifying risk factor.

sections.heading: Frequency and Duration
sections.text:
The following frequency and duration limits apply:
Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 23 months.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements
sections.text:
The medical record must support the medical necessity of each service.
When bone mass measurement continues beyond the initial period, the record must document measurable improvement. Documentation must identify the practitioner who performed or supervised each scan. Progress notes must document the beneficiary's response to each scan.

sections.heading: Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
sections.text:
The following qualifications apply:
Facilities furnishing bone mass measurement must maintain written protocols for emergency response. The interpreting practitioner must be board certified in radiology. Bone mass measurement must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: ICD-10-CM Codes that Support Medical Necessity
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
- E28.310 - Symptomatic premature menopause
- M81.0 - Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
- Z79.52 - Long term (current) use of systemic steroids
- Z87.310 - Personal history of (healed) osteoporosis fracture

sections.heading: Billing Instructions
sections.text:
1. Claims submitted without the ordering practitioner's National Provider Identifier will be rejected.
2. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the scan was furnished.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text:
- Fictional Society of Radiology. Clinical practice guideline for osteoporosis. 2021 edition.
- Example Journal of Radiology. Outcomes of bone mass measurement in older adults. 2014.

sections.heading: Policy Contact
sections.text: Inquiries may be submitted to the fictional contractor medical review department at (555) 0134-3569.
